In the right grid, the same multiplication-table format is shown, but the top column headers and left row headers are blank. The visible product entries are 35 and 63 in the upper product row, and 30 and ? in the lower product row. Reasoning: Since 35 and 63 are in the same row of a multiplication table, they share the same row factor. A common row factor that works is 7, because 35 = 7 × 5 and 63 = 7 × 9. So the two column factors are 5 and 9. The lower row has 30 under the first column factor 5, so the lower row factor is 6 because 30 = 6 × 5. Therefore the missing entry is 6 × 9 = 54.
